passage.text: Many people believe that creativity is a gift: either you are born creative, or you are not.
passage.reading: ˈmɛni ˈpiːpəl bɪˈliːv ðæt ˌkriːeɪˈtɪvəti ɪz ə ˈɡɪft: ˈiːðər juː ər ˈbɔːrn kriˈeɪtɪv, ɔːr juː ər ˈnɑːt.

passage.text: We often think of famous artists and inventors as geniuses who were different from everyone else.
passage.reading: wiː ˈɔːfən ˈθɪŋk əv ˈfeɪməs ˈɑːrtɪsts ənd ɪnˈvɛntərz əz ˈdʒiːniəsɪz huː wɜːr ˈdɪfərənt frəm ˈɛvriwʌn ˈɛls.

passage.text: Research shows that creativity does not come from one special part of the brain.
passage.reading: ˈriːsɜːrtʃ ˈʃoʊz ðæt ˌkriːeɪˈtɪvəti dʌz ˈnɑːt ˈkʌm frəm ˈwʌn ˈspɛʃəl ˈpɑːrt əv ðə ˈbreɪn.

passage.text: Instead, different parts of the brain work together when we have new ideas.
passage.reading: ɪnˈstɛd, ˈdɪfərənt ˈpɑːrts əv ðə ˈbreɪn ˈwɜːrk təˈɡɛðər wɛn wiː ˈhæv ˈnuː aɪˈdiːəz.

passage.text: This means that creativity is not only for artists.
passage.reading: ðɪs ˈmiːnz ðæt ˌkriːeɪˈtɪvəti ɪz ˈnɑːt ˈoʊnli fər ˈɑːrtɪsts.

passage.text: Scientists, engineers and business people use it every day for problem-solving.
passage.reading: ˈsaɪəntɪsts, ˌɛndʒɪˈnɪrz ənd ˈbɪznəs ˈpiːpəl ˈjuːz ɪt ˈɛvri ˈdeɪ fər ˈprɑːbləm ˌsɑːlvɪŋ.

passage.text: Research also suggests that people can become more creative with practice.
passage.reading: ˈriːsɜːrtʃ ˈɔːlsoʊ səɡˈdʒɛsts ðæt ˈpiːpəl kən bɪˈkʌm ˈmɔːr kriˈeɪtɪv wɪð ˈpræktɪs.

passage.text: For example, people who practice thinking of different ways to use a simple thing, like a cup, often get better at it.
passage.reading: fər ɪɡˈzæmpəl, ˈpiːpəl huː ˈpræktɪs ˈθɪŋkɪŋ əv ˈdɪfərənt ˈweɪz tə ˈjuːz ə ˈsɪmpəl ˈθɪŋ, ˈlaɪk ə ˈkʌp, ˈɔːfən ˈɡɛt ˈbɛtər ət ɪt.

passage.text: Children are naturally curious, and they ask a lot of questions.
passage.reading: ˈtʃɪldrən ər ˈnætʃərəli ˈkjʊriəs, ənd ðeɪ ˈæsk ə ˈlɑːt əv ˈkwɛstʃənz.

passage.text: Many experts believe that schools should encourage children to stay curious instead of only asking them to remember facts.
passage.reading: ˈmɛni ˈɛkspɜːrts bɪˈliːv ðæt ˈskuːlz ʃʊd ɪnˈkɜːrɪdʒ ˈtʃɪldrən tə ˈsteɪ ˈkjʊriəs ɪnˈstɛd əv ˈoʊnli ˈæskɪŋ ðɛm tə rɪˈmɛmbər ˈfækts.

passage.text: So, can anyone become a genius?
passage.reading: soʊ, kən ˈɛniwʌn bɪˈkʌm ə ˈdʒiːniəs?

passage.text: Probably not, but most scientists agree that everyone can become more creative.
passage.reading: ˈprɑːbəbli ˈnɑːt, bʌt ˈmoʊst ˈsaɪəntɪsts əˈɡriː ðæt ˈɛvriwʌn kən bɪˈkʌm ˈmɔːr kriˈeɪtɪv.

passage.text: Try new things, ask questions, and don't be afraid of making mistakes.
passage.reading: ˈtraɪ ˈnuː ˈθɪŋz, ˈæsk ˈkwɛstʃənz, ənd ˈdoʊnt bi əˈfreɪd əv ˈmeɪkɪŋ mɪˈsteɪks.

passage.text: Creativity, it seems, is more like a muscle than a gift: the more you use it, the stronger it gets.
passage.reading: ˌkriːeɪˈtɪvəti, ɪt ˈsiːmz, ɪz ˈmɔːr ˈlaɪk ə ˈmʌsəl ðən ə ˈɡɪft: ðə ˈmɔːr juː ˈjuːz ɪt, ðə ˈstrɔːŋɡər ɪt ˈɡɛts.
